title: Eugenio Monti Lends His Bolt
text:
At the 1964 Winter Olympics in Innsbruck, Austria, Eugenio Monti of Italy was the greatest bobsled driver in the world, with several world titles but no Olympic gold. In the two-man event, the British pair Tony Nash and Robin Dixon discovered that a bolt on their sled's rear axle had broken. Without it they were out of the competition.

Monti had already made his run. He took the bolt from his own sled and had it sent up to the top of the track for the British. They fitted it, raced, and won the gold medal. Monti and his partner took bronze.

In the four-man event Monti helped again, when his mechanics repaired the damaged axle of the Canadian sled. The Canadians won gold; Monti's Italian team took bronze. Criticized in the Italian press, Monti said the British had won because they were the fastest, not because of his bolt.

He was widely honored for sportsmanship. Four years later, at Grenoble in 1968, Monti finally won Olympic gold in both the two-man and four-man events.
lesson: Real competitors want to beat the best at their best, not a rival crippled by bad luck. Helping an opponent compete fairly costs little and gains lasting respect.
people: Eugenio Monti, Tony Nash, Robin Dixon
source: Official reports of the IX Olympic Winter Games, Innsbruck (1964); contemporary press reports
